verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch four astronauts around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day trip around the moon'; R3: 'The crew includes Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen'; R4: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, as well as Jeremy Hansen ... will set off to orbit the Moon'; R5: 'Artemis II is planned to send four astronauts on a lunar flyby'; R6: 'Three NASA astronauts and a Canadian astronaut will venture around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state four astronauts on a mission around/orbiting/flyby of the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launch attempt on April 1' in context of March 30, 2026; R4: 'launch date for NASA’s Artemis II is either April 1 or April 2, 2026'; R5: 'Artemis II (NET April 1, 2026)', 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026)'; R6: 'NASA's Artemis II ... scheduled to launch on Wednesday, April 1' (article dated March 30, 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm April 1, 2026, as the scheduled date.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Liftoff is set for 6:24 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'Launch: 6:24 p.m.'; R7: 'targeted launch time of 6:24 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time '6:24 p.m. EDT' directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch from Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla.'; R4: 'Kennedy Space Center’s LC-39B'; R5: 'from the Kennedy Space Center'; R6: 'Location: Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center'; R7: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly specify Pad 39B (LC-39B) at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four astronauts on a 10-day trip'; R4: 'orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission'; R5: '10 days'; R6: '10-day flight'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm 10-day duration and crewed nature.

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA’s new moon rocket blasted off ... Artemis I' (2022 context); R3: 'Artemis II builds on the success of the uncrewed Artemis I in 2022'; R4: 'ahead of the uncrewed Artemis I launch' (2022); R5: 'Artemis I (November 16, 2022) was the first uncrewed test flight'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis I was uncrewed, successful, in 2022, and Artemis II follows it.
